problem: Side gap NOT fixed: it still flips with bot skill, and the strategic mirror is ~19 points apart
evidence: Treasurer win rate by equal-skill mirror (2,000 games each): random 60.2%, greedy 35.3%, strategic 40.5% (second strategic mirror run 44.0%; plus-bot mirror 38.9-42.0%). Seat gap (2x deviation, same definition as before) is 9.3 on the 3-mirror average only because random (+20) cancels greedy (-29) and strategic (-19). Mixed: strategic T vs strategic W 40.5, strategic T beats random W 64.8%, random T loses to strategic W 80.5%. Previous: 10.9 (58/38/38). Target <= 5 in the strategic mirror and <= 10 across mirrors.
fix: The Whisperer is the skill side. Tested single levers (2,000 games each, mirror Treasurer win random/greedy/strategic/plus): Whisper 5->4: 62/35/46/43; Gold Purse 4->5: 63/34/42/43; Treasury cap 3: 57/36/42/43 vs cap 2: 57/35/41/42. Whisper 4 gives the best strategic gain (+4) but not enough alone. Bigger lever needed on the Whisperer side (fewer Hush cards, or Hush cannot target the highest card, or Retort needs a cost), or accept an explicit side-swap rule (play two games, swap sides) and say so.

problem: The designer's keyword ablations mostly fail: Spend, Steady and Echo are inert; Hush and Retort are below the 5-point bar
evidence: Ablation bot vs full 'plus' bot on same side (2,000 games, full bot's mirror T 38.9%): never-Spend -0.1 pts (needs >=5), ignore-Steady -0.9, no-Echo-throw -3.1 (the ablation does BETTER), random Hush target +3.1 (win loss), never-Retort +1.9. Spend used 1.2 times per game. Treasury cap 2 vs 3 changes the strategic mirror by about 1-2 points (noise), so the 'one knob' barely moves anything.
fix: Either the bots do not exploit these keywords (cannot rule out: the 'plus' bot is a heuristic) or the keywords are decoration. Rework Spend (+2 per coin is rarely worth the lost card) and Steady, or cut them and save rule budget.

problem: Court draws do not move lead changes for the skilled bot
evidence: Court draws off: strategic mirror lead changes 2.63 vs 2.54 with draws on (+0.09 only, design asked >= 0.3); greedy 1.32 vs 1.89 and random 1.52 vs 2.09 do gain (+0.57). Lead changes come from the track having no centre, not from the court.
fix: Keep or remove the court draws knowingly; the L3 'comeback' claim is carried by the track shape. Early leader after round 2 wins only 44.1% (below 50%: trailing is not a handicap), so there is no runaway at all.

problem: Round 1 hand-dump and tiny later rounds
evidence: Narrated game: Treasurer empties 6 cards for a 20-16 win, then rounds 2-4 are decided by 1-card totals (T0 W1, T2 W1, T1 W2). Mean 40 plays per game; 5.7 rounds; 14.8% of mirror games end by round 3.
fix: Minor now (all-pairing by-round-3 is 18.5%, target < 20: PASS, but only just). A hand limit or smaller draws would stop the feast-famine pattern; untested.

problem: The Whisper and Chancellor's Seal remain strong outliers
evidence: Whisper played in 81% of games, rounds with it +20.3 pts over the Whisperer average; Seal 77% played, +22.8 pts. Both flagged 'strong' (both rounds are the ones where they win, partly selection).
fix: Whisper to 4 is the held-back lever 3; tested above, +4 for the Treasurer in the strategic mirror.
